angularDiameterSource: Evans et al. (2024, ApJ 971, 190; arXiv:2407.09641, Section III.1): mean limb-darkened diameter 3.143 +/- 0.027 mas and linear limb-darkening coefficient 0.120 +/- 0.043 from CHARA/MIRC and MIRC-X H-band squared visibilities of 2016-2021, after dividing MIRC-X sizes by the wavelength-scale factor 1.0054.
distanceSource: 136.90 +/- 0.34 pc, the distance Evans et al. (2024, ApJ 971, 190) adopt: the Gaia DR3 parallax of the wide companion Polaris B (7.2869 +/- 0.0178 mas via SIMBAD) with the Lindegren zero-point offset. Polaris Aa itself is too bright for a reliable Gaia parallax; Hipparcos gives 7.54 mas (133 pc).
radiusSource: The Evans et al. (2024) diameter at their adopted distance: 3.143 mas at 136.90 pc is 32,184,239 km, 46.26 solar radii at 695700 km; the paper gives 46.27 +/- 0.42 solar radii.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Effective temperature 6015 ± 170 K from Usenko et al. 2005 (MNRAS 362, 1219; https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1365-2966.2005.09353.x), abstract: the mean spectroscopic temperature from 30 spectra of 2001-2004. Polaris is a low-amplitude Cepheid; the ± may be the spread over its 3.97-day pulsation.
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the astronomy record's GM and radius (physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, shown in the shared neutral gray because no image of the photosphere is cast here (see investigations.json). The photosphere of a pulsating supergiant is not a solid surface and its limb is not sharp.
